method_notes: Breadth-first census of UK concert halls, theatres and auditoria with capacity >= 1,000 across all four nations, compiled 2026-09-20 from pages actually fetched in-session. Most capacities are GRADE_B (Wikipedia article wikitext retrieved via the MediaWiki API; the exact API URL fetched is cited as capacity_source), with GRADE_A first-party confirmation where a venue or operator site could be fetched (e.g. Usher Hall 2,200 from cultureedinburgh.com, Sheffield City Hall operator from sheffieldcityhall.co.uk). Roughly 22 candidate venues were verified to be under 1,000 and excluded: 19 West End houses (Ambassadors 444, Apollo 658, Arts 350, Criterion 588, Duchess 494, Fortune 432, Garrick 718, Gielgud 994, Harold Pinter 796, Lyric 915, Noel Coward 942, Playhouse 550, @sohoplace 602, St Martin’s 550, Theatre Royal Haymarket 888, Tom Stoppard 640, Trafalgar 630, Vaudeville 690, Wyndham’s 799) plus Eden Court Empire Theatre 840, Dundee Rep c.455 and Theatr Clwyd 570; numerous sub-1,000 studio/second spaces inside included complexes (Lilian Baylis 200, Sage Two 600, Barbican Pit 200, Lyttelton 890, Dorfman 400, Spa Theatre 675, Sheffield Memorial Hall 500 and others) are noted in capacity_configuration rather than listed separately. Known limitations: several official sites (royalalberthall.com, southbankcentre.co.uk, lwtheatres.co.uk, trafalgarentertainment.com) returned 403/404/bot-detection so no first-party evidence was obtained for them; capacities marked CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED are venues confirmed to exist on a fetched operator directory but whose size was not verified, and Theatre Royal Brighton in particular may prove sub-1,000 on review. St David’s Hall Cardiff is recorded with operational_status STATUS_REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than OPERATIONAL because the fetched Wikipedia article states it closed in September 2023 due to RAAC in the roof and was "not expected to reopen until 2026" — whether it has now reopened was not verified.
